questions.questionText: Chords AB and CD of a circle, when produced, meet at a point P outside the circle. If $AB = 6\text{ cm}$, $CD = 3\text{ cm}$ and $PD = 5\text{ cm}$, then PB is equal to:
questions.solution:
$PC = PD + CD = 5 + 3 = 8\text{ cm}$.
$PA = PB + 6$.
$PA \times PB = PC \times PD \implies (PB + 6)PB = 8 \times 5 = 40$.
$PB^2 + 6PB - 40 = 0 \implies (PB - 4)(PB + 10) = 0 \implies PB = 4\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: XAB and XCD are two secants to a circle. If $XA = 18\text{ cm}$, $AB = 22\text{ cm}$ and $XC = 24\text{ cm}$, then find the value of XD (in cm).
questions.solution:
$XB = XA + AB = 18 + 22 = 40\text{ cm}$.
$XA \times XB = XC \times XD \implies 18 \times 40 = 24 \times XD \implies XD = \frac{720}{24} = 30\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: A secant PAB is drawn from an external point P to the circle with the centre at O, intersecting it at A and B. If $OP = 17\text{ cm}$, $PA = 12\text{ cm}$ and $PB = 22.5\text{ cm}$, then the radius of the circle is:
questions.solution:
Power of point $P$: $PA \times PB = OP^2 - R^2$.
$12 \times 22.5 = 17^2 - R^2 \implies 270 = 289 - R^2 \implies R^2 = 19 \implies R = \sqrt{19}\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: Chords AB and CD of a circle, when produced, meet at the point P. If $AB = 6.3\text{ cm}$, $BP = 4.5\text{ cm}$, and $CD = 3.6\text{ cm}$, then the length (in cm) of PD is
questions.solution:
$PA = AB + BP = 6.3 + 4.5 = 10.8\text{ cm}$.
$PA \times PB = PC \times PD \implies 10.8 \times 4.5 = (PD + 3.6)PD$.
$PD^2 + 3.6PD - 48.6 = 0 \implies PD = 5.4\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: R is a point outside a circle and is 18 cm away from its centre. A secant drawn from the point R intersects the circle at points A and B in such a way that $RA = 7\text{ cm}$ and $AB = 5\text{ cm}$. The radius of the circle (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
$RB = RA + AB = 7 + 5 = 12\text{ cm}$.
$RA \times RB = OR^2 - r^2 \implies 7 \times 12 = 18^2 - r^2 \implies 84 = 324 - r^2 \implies r^2 = 240$.
$r = \sqrt{240} = 4\sqrt{15}\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: In a circle, two chords AB and CD intersect each other internally at point P. If $AB = 16\text{ cm}$, $PB = 6\text{ cm}$ and $PD = 12\text{ cm}$, then the value of PC (in cm) is equal to:
questions.solution:
$AP = AB - PB = 16 - 6 = 10\text{ cm}$.
$AP \times PB = CP \times PD \implies 10 \times 6 = PC \times 12 \implies PC = 5\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: In a circle, chords AB and CD intersect internally at E. If $CD = 18\text{ cm}$, $AE = 13\text{ cm}$, then the length of BE is:
questions.solution:
Let $CE = x$, so $ED = 18 - x$.
By chord intersection: $AE \times BE = CE \times ED \implies 13 \times BE = x(18 - x)$.
For integer options, when $BE = 5\text{ cm}$, $x(18 - x) = 65 \implies x^2 - 18x + 65 = 0 \implies (x - 5)(x - 13) = 0$, which has real integer roots $5$ and $13$.
Thus, $BE = 5\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: In a circle, the chords AB and CD intersect each other at point L (internally). If $AL = 9\text{ cm}$, $LB = 7\text{ cm}$ and $LD = 3\text{ cm}$, then find CL (in cm).
questions.solution: $AL \times LB = CL \times LD \implies 9 \times 7 = CL \times 3 \implies CL = \frac{63}{3} = 21\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: O is the centre of the circle. Its two chord AB and CD intersect each other at the point P (internally) within the circle. If $AB = 22\text{ cm}$, $PB = 14\text{ cm}$, $CP = 8\text{ cm}$, then find the value of the PD
questions.solution:
$AP = AB - PB = 22 - 14 = 8\text{ cm}$.
By intersecting chords theorem: $AP \times PB = CP \times PD$.
$8 \times 14 = 8 \times PD \implies PD = 14\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: In a circle, two chords MN and PQ intersect at O. If $MO = 9\text{ cm}$, $ON = 5\text{ cm}$ and $OQ = 6\text{ cm}$, then the value of OP (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
By intersecting chords theorem: $MO \times ON = OP \times OQ$.
$9 \times 5 = OP \times 6 \implies OP = \frac{45}{6} = 7.5\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: Chords $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{CD}$ of a circle intersect inside the circle at point F. If $(AF) = 2.4\text{ cm}$, $m(\overline{BF}) = 1.8\text{ cm}$, and $m(\overline{CD}) = 5.7\text{ cm}$. What is the length (in cm) of the longer of the two line segments, (CF) and (DF)?
questions.solution:
$AF \times BF = CF \times DF = 2.4 \times 1.8 = 4.32$.
Also, $CF + DF = 5.7$.
Let the segments be $x$ and $5.7 - x$:
$x(5.7 - x) = 4.32 \implies x^2 - 5.7x + 4.32 = 0$.
Solving gives $x = 4.8\text{ cm}$ and $x = 0.9\text{ cm}$.
The longer segment is $4.8\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: The diameter PQ of a circle with centre O is perpendicular to the chord RS. PQ intersects RS at T. If $RS = 16\text{ cm}$ and $QT = 4\text{ cm}$, what is the length (in cm) of the diameter of the circle?
questions.solution:
Diameter $PQ \perp RS$ at $T$, so $T$ bisects $RS$, giving $RT = TS = 8\text{ cm}$.
By intersecting chords: $PT \times QT = RT \times TS$.
$PT \times 4 = 8 \times 8 = 64 \implies PT = 16\text{ cm}$.
Diameter $PQ = PT + QT = 16 + 4 = 20\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: JKLM is a cyclic quadrilateral in which $\angle K$ is opposite to $\angle M$. When JK and ML are produced, meet at point Z. $JK = 10\text{ cm}$, $KZ = 12\text{ cm}$ and $MZ = 33\text{ cm}$. What is the length of LZ?
questions.solution:
$ZJ = JK + KZ = 10 + 12 = 22\text{ cm}$.
By secant property of cyclic quadrilateral: $ZK \times ZJ = ZL \times ZM$.
$12 \times 22 = ZL \times 33 \implies ZL = \frac{264}{33} = 8\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: A sector of a circle has a central angle of $45^\circ$ and an arc length of 22 cm. Find the radius of the circle. (Use $\pi = 22/7$)
questions.solution:
Arc length $L = \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times 2\pi r$.
$22 = \frac{45^\circ}{360^\circ} \times 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r \implies 22 = \frac{1}{8} \times \frac{44}{7} r \implies r = 28\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: In a circle of radius 14 cm, an arc subtends an angle of $90^\circ$ at the centre. The length of arc (in cm) is equal to: (Take $\pi = 22/7$)
questions.solution: Arc length $= \frac{90^\circ}{360^\circ} \times 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 14 = \frac{1}{4} \times 88 = 22\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: In a circle, an arc subtends an angle of $84^\circ$ at the centre. If the length of the arc is 22 cm, then the radius of the circle (in cm) is equal to: (Take $\pi = 22/7$)
questions.solution:
Arc length $= \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times 2\pi r$.
$22 = \frac{84^\circ}{360^\circ} \times 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r \implies 1 = \frac{7}{30} \times \frac{2}{7} r \implies r = 15\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: From a circle of radius 7 units, an arc length is cut by a chord of length 7 units. What is the arc length of the smaller portion (in units)?
questions.solution:
Since chord length equals the radius, the triangle formed with the centre is equilateral, so $\theta = 60^\circ$.
Arc length $= \frac{60^\circ}{360^\circ} \times 2\pi(7) = \frac{7}{3}\pi\text{ units}$.

questions.questionText: At what angle is the arc length half the perimeter of the circle?
questions.solution:
Arc length is half the perimeter when it spans a semicircle:
$\frac{\theta}{360^\circ} = \frac{1}{2} \implies \theta = 180^\circ$.

questions.questionText: Find the number of common tangents, if $r_1 + r_2 = C_1C_2$.(With usual notations, $r_1$ & $r_2$ and $C_1$ & $C_2$ are the radii and centres of the two circles.)
questions.solution:
When the distance between the centres equals the sum of the radii ($C_1C_2 = r_1 + r_2$), the two circles touch each other externally.
Two externally touching circles have exactly 3 common tangents.

questions.questionText: If two circles do not touch or intersect each other and one does not lie inside the other, then find the number of common tangents.
questions.solution: Two separate, non-intersecting circles have 4 common tangents (2 direct common tangents and 2 transverse common tangents).

questions.questionText: Two circles with centres P and Q of radii 6 cm and 4 cm, respectively, touch each other internally. If the perpendicular bisector of PQ meets the bigger circle at A and B, then the value of AB is:
questions.solution:
Distance between centres $PQ = R - r = 6 - 4 = 2\text{ cm}$.
The perpendicular bisector of $PQ$ passes through the midpoint of $PQ$, at distance $d = \frac{2}{2} = 1\text{ cm}$ from $P$.
Half-length of chord $AB = \sqrt{R^2 - d^2} = \sqrt{6^2 - 1^2} = \sqrt{35}\text{ cm}$.
$AB = 2\sqrt{35}\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: A line cuts two concentric circles. The length of chords formed by this line on the circles is 6 cm and 18 cm. Find the difference in the squares of the radii of two circles.
questions.solution:
Let $d$ be the perpendicular distance from the centre to the secant line.
$R^2 = d^2 + 9^2 = d^2 + 81$
$r^2 = d^2 + 3^2 = d^2 + 9$
$R^2 - r^2 = 81 - 9 = 72$.

questions.questionText: Two circles of diameters 16 cm and 20 cm are such that the distance between their centers is 13 cm. What is the length (in cm) of a common tangent to these circles that does not intersect the line joining the centers?
questions.solution:
Radii are $r_1 = 8\text{ cm}$ and $r_2 = 10\text{ cm}$. Distance between centres $d = 13\text{ cm}$.
A common tangent that does not intersect the line of centres is a direct common tangent (DCT):
$\text{DCT} = \sqrt{d^2 - (r_2 - r_1)^2} = \sqrt{13^2 - (10 - 8)^2} = \sqrt{169 - 4} = \sqrt{165}\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: Two circles of radii 3 units and r units, respectively, have a 6 units distance between their centers. If the length of the direct common tangent is $\sqrt{35}$ units, then the value of r is ___ units.
questions.solution:
$\text{DCT}^2 = d^2 - (r - 3)^2$.
$35 = 6^2 - (r - 3)^2 \implies (r - 3)^2 = 36 - 35 = 1 \implies |r - 3| = 1$.
$r = 4$ or $r = 2$. From the given options, $r = 4\text{ units}$.

questions.questionText: The length (in cm) of a direct common tangent to two circles of radii 14 cm and 5 cm whose centres are separated by a distance of 40 cm is:

The length of a common external tangent to two circles of an equal radius of 5 units is equal to the diameter of the circle. Which of the following can be the distance between the centres of the circles in units?
questions.solution:
For equal radii $r_1 = r_2 = 5$, $\text{DCT} = \sqrt{d^2 - 0} = d$.
Since $\text{DCT} = \text{diameter} = 2 \times 5 = 10\text{ units}$, the distance between centres $d = 10\text{ units}$.

questions.questionText: The centres of two circles are 84 cm apart, If the radii of these two circles are 38 cm and 26 cm, respectively. then which of the following options gives the length (in cm) of a direct common tangent of these two circles?
The distance between the centres of two circles is 81 cm, and their radius are 42 cm and 51 cm. What is the length (in cm) of the direct common tangent to the circles?
A and B are centres of two circles of radii 32 cm and 8 cm, respectively. CD is a direct common tangent to the circles. If the length of AB = 30 cm, then the length of CD will be:

In two circles centred at O and O', the distance between the centres of both circles is 17 cm. The points of contact of a direct common tangent between the circles are P and Q. If the radii of both circles are 7 cm and 15 cm, respectively, then the length of PQ is equal to:
A direct common tangent is drawn to two circles of radius 25 cm and 20 cm. The centres of the two circles are 35 cm apart. What is the length (in cm) of the tangent?
The distance between the centres of two circles having radii of 24 cm and 18 cm, respectively, is 48 cm. find the length (in cm) of a direct common tangent to the two circles.
M and N are, respectively, the centres of two circles of radii 12 cm and 8 cm. QR is the common tangent to the circles. If $MN = 16\text{ cm}$, then what will be the length of QR?
For two circles of radius 7 units and $\frac{7}{2}$ units, whose centres are 15 units apart, what is the length of the direct common tangent in units? (Correct to 3 decimal places.)
R wishes to use a stick of length 6 units as common internal tangent to two circles of radius two units and three units. What can be the maximum distance (in units) between the centres of the circle?
questions.solution: $\text{TCT} = \sqrt{d^2 - (r_1 + r_2)^2} \implies 6 = \sqrt{d^2 - (2 + 3)^2} \implies 36 = d^2 - 25 \implies d = \sqrt{61}\text{ units}$.

questions.questionText: R wishes to use a stick of length 6 units as common internal tangent to two circles of radius two units and three units. What can be the maximum distance (in units) between the centres of the circle?
questions.solution: $\text{TCT} = \sqrt{d^2 - (r_1 + r_2)^2} \implies 6 = \sqrt{d^2 - 5^2} \implies 36 = d^2 - 25 \implies d = \sqrt{61}\text{ units}$.

questions.questionText: R wishes to use a stick of length 6 units as common internal tangent to two circles of radius two units and three units. What can be the maximum distance (in units) between the centres of the circle?
questions.solution: $\text{TCT} = \sqrt{d^2 - (r_1 + r_2)^2} \implies 6 = \sqrt{d^2 - 5^2} \implies d^2 = 61 \implies d = \sqrt{61}\text{ units}$.

questions.questionText: The radii of two circle are 5 cm and 10 cm and the distance between their centres is 17 cm. Find the length of the transverse common tangent.
The distance between the centres of two circles of radii 7 cm and 5 cm is 15 cm. Find the length of the transverse common tangent to these circles.
The radii of the two circles are 7 cm and 4 cm. If the distance between their centres is 25 cm, then the length of the transverse common tangent is equal to:
If the radii of two circles are 6 cm and 3 cm and the length of the transverse common tangent is 8 cm, then the distance between the two circles is:
The distance between the centres of two circle of radii 4 cm, and 2 cm is 10 cm. The length (in cm) of a transverse common tangent is:
The distance between the centres of the two circles, with radii 3 cm and 2 cm, respectively, is 13 cm. The length (in cm) of a transverse common tangent is:
What is the length (in cm) of the transverse common tangent between two circles with radii 6 cm and 4 cm, given that the distance between their centres is 14 cm?
If the radius of two circles be 6 cm and 9 cm and the length of the transverse common tangent be 20 cm, then find the distance between the two centres.
If the distance between the centres of two circles is 12cm and the radii are 5 cm and 4 cm, then the length (in cm) of the transverse common tangent is:
If the sum of the radii and the distance between the centers of two circles are equal, then:
questions.solution: When the distance between the centres equals the sum of their radii ($d = r_1 + r_2$), the circles touch externally.

questions.questionText: Two circles touch each other at a point O. AB is a simple common tangent to both the circles touching at point A and point B. If radii of the circles are 9 cm and 4 cm, then find AB.
questions.solution:
For two circles touching externally, the length of the direct common tangent is:
$AB = 2\sqrt{r_1 r_2} = 2\sqrt{9 \times 4} = 2 \times 6 = 12\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: Two circles of radii 16 cm and 4 cm, respectively, touch each other externally at Point A. PQ is the direct common tangent of these circles with centres $C_1$ and $C_2$, respectively. What is the length of PQ?
questions.solution: $PQ = 2\sqrt{r_1 r_2} = 2\sqrt{16 \times 4} = 2 \times 8 = 16\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: Two circles touch each other externally as shown in the figure above. The radius of the circle with centre O is 49 cm. The radius of the circle with centre A is 16 cm. Find the length (in cm) of their common tangent BC.
questions.solution: $BC = 2\sqrt{r_1 r_2} = 2\sqrt{49 \times 16} = 2 \times 7 \times 4 = 56\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: Two circles touch each other externally. The radius of the first circle with centre A is 18 cm. The radius of the second circle with centre B is 8 cm. Find the length of their common tangent CD.
questions.solution: $CD = 2\sqrt{r_1 r_2} = 2\sqrt{18 \times 8} = 2\sqrt{144} = 24\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: In the following figure, there are two circles that touch each other externally. The radius of the first circle with centre P is 25 cm. The radius of the second circle with centre Q is 4 cm. Find the length of their direct common tangent AB.
questions.solution: $AB = 2\sqrt{r_1 r_2} = 2\sqrt{25 \times 4} = 2\sqrt{100} = 20\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: There are two circles touching each other externally. The radius of the first circle with centre O is 12 cm. The radius of the second circle with centre A is 5 cm. Find the length of their common tangent touching the two circles at points P and Q.
questions.solution: $PQ = 2\sqrt{r_1 r_2} = 2\sqrt{12 \times 5} = 2\sqrt{60} = 4\sqrt{15}\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: Two circles with centre O and A touch each other externally. The radius of the first circle with centre O is 6 cm. The radius of the second circle with centre A is 3 cm. Find the length of their common tangent CB (in centimetres).
questions.solution: $CB = 2\sqrt{r_1 r_2} = 2\sqrt{6 \times 3} = 2\sqrt{18} = 6\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: Two circles of radii 18 cm and 12 cm touch each other externally. Find the length (in cm) of their direct common tangent.
questions.solution: $\text{DCT} = 2\sqrt{r_1 r_2} = 2\sqrt{18 \times 12} = 2\sqrt{216} = 12\sqrt{6}\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: If two circles of radii 35 cm and 25 cm touch each other externally, then the length (in cm) of a common tangent is (Rounded off to 2 decimal places)
questions.solution: $\text{DCT} = 2\sqrt{35 \times 25} = 10\sqrt{35} \approx 10 \times 5.91608 = 59.16\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: Two circles $C_1$ and $C_2$ touch each other externally. The radius of $C_1 = 16\text{ cm}$ and the radius of $C_2 = 8\text{ cm}$. Find the length (in cm) of their common tangent.
questions.solution: $\text{DCT} = 2\sqrt{16 \times 8} = 2\sqrt{128} = 16\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: A bigger circle centre at O and a smaller circle centre at P touch each other externally such that the length of their common tangent LM is 12 cm. If the radius of the bigger circle is 18 cm, then what will be the radius (in cm) of the smaller circle?
questions.solution: $LM = 2\sqrt{R r} \implies 12 = 2\sqrt{18 r} \implies 6 = \sqrt{18 r} \implies 36 = 18 r \implies r = 2\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: The length of the common tangent $PQ$ for two circles touching externally is $16\text{ cm}$. If the radius ($OP$) of the bigger circle is $20\text{ cm}$, then the radius ($RQ$) of the smaller circle is:
questions.solution:
For two externally touching circles, direct common tangent length is $L = 2\sqrt{r_1 r_2}$.
$$16 = 2\sqrt{20 \times r_2} \implies 8 = \sqrt{20 r_2} \implies 64 = 20 r_2 \implies r_2 = 3.2\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: Two circles with centres $M$ and $N$ have radii $5\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$ respectively. The circles touch each other externally at point $T$. A line $PR$ is drawn such that the points $M, T$ and $N$ lie on $PR$, $P$ being closer to $M$. From $P$, a tangent $PQ = 12\text{ cm}$ is drawn to the circle with centre $M$ touching at $Q$, and from $R$, another tangent $RS = 15\text{ cm}$ is drawn to circle with centre $N$ touching at $S$. What is the length (in $\text{cm}$) of $PR$?
questions.solution:
In $\triangle PQM$, $PM = \sqrt{PQ^2 + r_1^2} = \sqrt{12^2 + 5^2} = 13\text{ cm}$.
In $\triangle RSN$, $RN = \sqrt{RS^2 + r_2^2} = \sqrt{15^2 + 8^2} = 17\text{ cm}$.
The distance $MN = r_1 + r_2 = 5 + 8 = 13\text{ cm}$.
Since $M, T, N$ lie on line $PR$ in order $P - M - T - N - R$:
$$PR = PM + MN + NR = 13 + 13 + 17 = 43\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: $P$ and $Q$ are centres of two circles whose radii are $7\text{ cm}$ and $3\text{ cm}$ respectively. If the direct common tangents to the circles meet $PQ$ extended at $A$, then $A$ divides $PQ$:
questions.solution: Direct common tangents intersect at the external center of similitude $A$, which divides the line joining centres $PQ$ externally in the ratio of their radii $r_1 : r_2 = 7 : 3$.

questions.questionText: The centres of two circles of radii $20\text{ cm}$ and $32\text{ cm}$ are $60\text{ cm}$ apart. What is the ratio of the length of the direct common tangent to the length of the transverse common tangent to these circles?
questions.solution:
Direct common tangent: $DCT = \sqrt{d^2 - (r_1 - r_2)^2} = \sqrt{60^2 - (32 - 20)^2} = \sqrt{3600 - 144} = \sqrt{3456} = 24\sqrt{6}$.
Transverse common tangent: $TCT = \sqrt{d^2 - (r_1 + r_2)^2} = \sqrt{60^2 - 52^2} = \sqrt{3600 - 2704} = \sqrt{896} = 8\sqrt{14}$.
Ratio $DCT : TCT = 24\sqrt{6} : 8\sqrt{14} = 3\sqrt{6} : \sqrt{14}$.

questions.questionText: The centers of two circles of radii $25\text{ cm}$ and $35\text{ cm}$ are $80\text{ cm}$ apart. What is the ratio of the lengths of the transverse common tangent to the direct common tangent to these circles?

The centres of two circles are $36\text{ cm}$ apart. If the radii of these two circles are $15\text{ cm}$ and $9\text{ cm}$, respectively, then what is the sum of the lengths (in $\text{cm}$) of a direct common tangent and a transverse common tangent of these two circles?
If the length of a common external tangent to two circles is $9$ and that of a common internal tangent is $5$, then the product of the radii of the two circles is:

Two circles with centers $B$ and $D$ have radii $DA = 8\text{ cm}$ and $BC = x\text{ cm}$, respectively. $AC$ is tangent to both circles. If $DB$ and $AC$ intersect at point $E$, $AE = 12\text{ cm}$ and $EC = 18\text{ cm}$, then find the value of $x$ (in $\text{cm}$).
questions.solution:
Since radii to tangent are perpendicular: $\triangle DAE \sim \triangle BCE$.
$$\frac{DA}{BC} = \frac{AE}{EC} \implies \frac{8}{x} = \frac{12}{18} = \frac{2}{3} \implies x = \frac{8 \times 3}{2} = 12\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: In the given figure, the circle with centre $O$ has radius $10\text{ cm}$. The radius of the circle with centre $P$ is $x\text{ cm}$. $STR$ is a common tangent to the two circles at points $R$ and $S$ as shown in the figures. $RT = 16\text{ cm}$ and $TS = 24\text{ cm}$. What is the value of $x$ (in $\text{cm}$)?
questions.solution:
By similar right triangles $\triangle ORT \sim \triangle PST$:
$$\frac{OR}{PS} = \frac{RT}{TS} \implies \frac{10}{x} = \frac{16}{24} = \frac{2}{3} \implies x = \frac{10 \times 3}{2} = 15\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: In the following figure, the circles with centres $B$ and $D$ have radius $4\text{ cm}$ and $x\text{ cm}$, respectively. $AC$ is a tangent to both the circles. Find the value of $x$.
questions.solution:
By similar triangles formed by radii and tangents from the intersection point:
$$\frac{r_1}{r_2} = \frac{d_1}{d_2} \implies x = 6\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: Two circles touch each other externally at $T$. $RS$ is a direct common tangent to the two circles touching the circles at $P$ and $Q$. If $\angle TPQ = 42^\circ$, then $\angle PQT$ (in degrees) is:
questions.solution:
The angle subtended by the direct common tangent chord at the point of external contact is always $\angle PTQ = 90^\circ$.
In $\triangle PTQ$:
$$\angle PQT = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 42^\circ = 48^\circ.$$

questions.questionText: Two circles touch each other externally at $C$. $AB$ is a direct common tangent to the two circles. $A$ and $B$ are points of contact and $\angle CAB = 55^\circ$. Then $\angle ACB$ is:
questions.solution: A known geometric property: When two circles touch externally, the direct common tangent subtends a right angle at the point of contact, so $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$.

questions.questionText: Two circles touch each other externally at $M$. $PQ$ is a direct common tangent to the two circles, $P$ and $Q$ are points of contact and $\angle MPQ = 38^\circ$. Then $\angle MQP$ is:
questions.solution:
Since $\angle PMQ = 90^\circ$:
$$\angle MQP = 90^\circ - 38^\circ = 52^\circ.$$

questions.questionText: Two circles intersect each other such that each passes through the centre of each other. Radius of these circles are equal. If the length of common chord is $14\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$, then what will be the sum of circumferences of these two circles?
questions.solution:
When two equal circles pass through each other's centres, common chord length is $L = r\sqrt{3}$.
$$r\sqrt{3} = 14\sqrt{3} \implies r = 14\text{ cm}.$$
Sum of circumferences $= 2 \times (2\pi r) = 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 14 = 4 \times 44 = 176\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: The length of the common chord of two intersecting circles is $24\text{ cm}$. If the diameter of the circles are $30\text{ cm}$ and $26\text{ cm}$, then the distance between the centres (in $\text{cm}$) is:
questions.solution:
Radii are $r_1 = 15\text{ cm}$, $r_2 = 13\text{ cm}$. Half chord is $12\text{ cm}$.
$d_1 = \sqrt{15^2 - 12^2} = \sqrt{225 - 144} = 9\text{ cm}$.
$d_2 = \sqrt{13^2 - 12^2} = \sqrt{169 - 144} = 5\text{ cm}$.
Distance between centres $d = d_1 + d_2 = 9 + 5 = 14\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: Two equal circles pass through each other's centre. If the radius of each of the circle is $13\text{ cm}$, then what is the length of the common chord?
questions.solution: Length of common chord $= r\sqrt{3} = 13\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: $PQ$ and $RS$ are common tangents to two circles intersecting at $A$ and $B$. $A$ and $B$, when produced on both the sides, meet the tangents $PQ$ and $RS$ at $X$ and $Y$, respectively. If $AB = 3\text{ cm}$ and $XY = 5\text{ cm}$, then $PQ$ is:
questions.solution: By tangent-secant theorem: $X$ and $Y$ are midpoints of tangents $PQ$ and $RS$, and $PQ = \sqrt{XY^2 - AB^2} = \sqrt{5^2 - 3^2} = 4\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: Two circles of radius $13\text{ cm}$ and $15\text{ cm}$ intersect each other at points $A$ and $B$. If the length of the common chord is $12\text{ cm}$, then what is the distance between their centres?

Two circles with diameters $50\text{ cm}$ and $58\text{ cm}$ respectively, intersect each other at points $A$ and $B$, such that the length of the common chord is $40\text{ cm}$. Find the distance (in $\text{cm}$) between the centres of these two circles.
questions.solution:
Radii are $r_1 = 25\text{ cm}$, $r_2 = 29\text{ cm}$. Half chord is $20\text{ cm}$.
$d_1 = \sqrt{25^2 - 20^2} = 15\text{ cm}$.
$d_2 = \sqrt{29^2 - 20^2} = \sqrt{841 - 400} = \sqrt{441} = 21\text{ cm}$.
Distance $= 15 + 21 = 36\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: Two circles of same radius $6\text{ cm}$ intersect each other at $P$ and $Q$. If $PQ = 10\text{ cm}$, then what is the distance between the centres of the circles?
questions.solution:
Half chord is $5\text{ cm}$.
Distance of each centre from chord $= \sqrt{6^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{36 - 25} = \sqrt{11}\text{ cm}$.
Distance between centres $= 2\sqrt{11}\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: Two circles having equal radius intersect each other such that each passes through the centre of the other. Length of the common chord is $24\text{ cm}$, then what will be the diameter of each circle?
questions.solution:
Common chord $L = r\sqrt{3} = 24 \implies r = \frac{24}{\sqrt{3}} = 8\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$.
Diameter $D = 2r = 16\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: Two circles having equal radius intersect each other such that each passes through the center of the other. Sum of diameter of these circles is $84\text{ cm}$, what is the length of the common chord?
questions.solution:
$2D = 84 \implies D = 42\text{ cm} \implies r = 21\text{ cm}$.
Common chord $L = r\sqrt{3} = 21\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: Two circles have radii of $27\text{ cm}$ and $36\text{ cm}$. The distance between their centres is $45\text{ cm}$. What is the length (in $\text{cm}$) of their common chord?
questions.solution:
Notice that $27^2 + 36^2 = 729 + 1296 = 2025 = 45^2$, so the triangle formed by centres and an intersection point is a right triangle with hypotenuse $45\text{ cm}$.
Altitude to hypotenuse (half chord) $h = \frac{27 \times 36}{45} = 21.6\text{ cm}$.
Length of common chord $= 2h = 43.2\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral in which $\angle B$ is opposite to $\angle D$. If $\angle B = x + 10^\circ$ and $\angle D = 2x + 35^\circ$, then what is the value of $x$?
questions.solution:
Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to $180^\circ$:
$$(x + 10^\circ) + (2x + 35^\circ) = 180^\circ \implies 3x + 45^\circ = 180^\circ \implies 3x = 135^\circ \implies x = 45^\circ.$$

questions.questionText: $PQRS$ is a cyclic quadrilateral. If $\angle P$ is three times of $\angle R$ and $\angle S$ is four times of $\angle Q$, then the sum of $\angle S + \angle R$ will be:
questions.solution:
$\angle P + \angle R = 180^\circ \implies 3\angle R + \angle R = 180^\circ \implies \angle R = 45^\circ$.
$\angle S + \angle Q = 180^\circ \implies 4\angle Q + \angle Q = 180^\circ \implies 5\angle Q = 180^\circ \implies \angle Q = 36^\circ \implies \angle S = 144^\circ$.
Sum $\angle S + \angle R = 144^\circ + 45^\circ = 189^\circ$.

questions.questionText: $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral. $AC$ and $BD$ intersect each other at $P$. If $AB = AC$ and $\angle BAC = 48^\circ$, then the measure of $\angle ADC$ is:
questions.solution:
In $\triangle ABC$, $AB = AC \implies \angle ABC = \angle ACB = \frac{180^\circ - 48^\circ}{2} = 66^\circ$.
In cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle ADC = 180^\circ - \angle ABC = 180^\circ - 66^\circ = 114^\circ$.

questions.questionText: $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral. Diagonals $BD$ and $AC$ intersect each other at $E$. If $\angle BEC = 138^\circ$ and $\angle ECD = 35^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle BAC$?
questions.solution:
In $\triangle CDE$, $\angle CED = 180^\circ - 138^\circ = 42^\circ$.
$\angle CDE = 180^\circ - (42^\circ + 35^\circ) = 103^\circ$.
Angles in the same segment: $\angle BAC = \angle BDC = \angle CDE = 103^\circ$.

questions.questionText: $\triangle ABC$ is inscribed in a circle with center $O$, such that $\angle ACB = 115^\circ$. $O$ is joined to $A$. What is the measure of $\angle OAB$?
questions.solution:
Reflex angle $\angle AOB = 2 \times 115^\circ = 230^\circ \implies \text{central } \angle AOB = 360^\circ - 230^\circ = 130^\circ$.
Since $OA = OB$, in isosceles $\triangle OAB$:
$$\angle OAB = \frac{180^\circ - 130^\circ}{2} = 25^\circ.$$

questions.questionText: $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral. Sides $AB$ and $DC$, when produced, meet at $E$ and sides $AD$ and $BC$ when produced, meet at $F$. If $\angle ADC = 76^\circ$ and $\angle AED = 55^\circ$, then $\angle AFB$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
In $\triangle ADE$, $\angle DAE = 180^\circ - 76^\circ - 55^\circ = 49^\circ$.
Since $ABCD$ is cyclic, $\angle BCD = 180^\circ - \angle BAD = 180^\circ - 49^\circ = 131^\circ \implies \angle DCF = 49^\circ$.
In $\triangle CDF$, $\angle F = 180^\circ - (76^\circ + 49^\circ) = 180^\circ - 125^\circ = 27^\circ$.

questions.questionText: Sides $AB$ and $DC$ of a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ are produced to meet at $E$ and sides $AD$ and $BC$ are produced to meet at $F$. If $\angle ADC = 78^\circ$ and $\angle BEC = 52^\circ$, then the measure of $\angle AFB$ is:
questions.solution:
In $\triangle ADE$, $\angle DAE = 180^\circ - 78^\circ - 52^\circ = 50^\circ$.
In cyclic quadrilateral, $\angle DCF = \angle A = 50^\circ$.
In $\triangle CDF$, $\angle AFB = 180^\circ - (78^\circ + 50^\circ) = 32^\circ$.

questions.questionText: $AB$ is a chord of a circle with centre $O$, $C$ is a point on the circumference of the circle in the minor sector. If $\angle ABO = 40^\circ$, what is the measure (in degree) of $\angle ACB$?
questions.solution:
In $\triangle AOB$, $OA = OB \implies \angle OAB = 40^\circ \implies \angle AOB = 180^\circ - 80^\circ = 100^\circ$.
Angle in major arc $= 50^\circ$.
Angle in minor arc $\angle ACB = 180^\circ - 50^\circ = 130^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In a circle, $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral in which $AE$ is drawn parallel to $CD$, and $BA$ is produced to $F$. If $\angle ABC = 85^\circ$ and $\angle FAE = 24^\circ$, find the value of $\angle BCD$?
questions.solution:
Since $ABCD$ is cyclic, $\angle ADC = 180^\circ - 85^\circ = 95^\circ$.
$AE \parallel CD \implies \angle DAE = 180^\circ - 95^\circ = 85^\circ$.
On line $FAB$: $\angle FAE + \angle EAD + \angle DAB = 180^\circ \implies 24^\circ + 85^\circ + \angle DAB = 180^\circ \implies \angle DAB = 71^\circ$.
Opposite angle $\angle BCD = 180^\circ - 71^\circ = 119^\circ$.

questions.questionText: An equilateral triangle $ABC$ is inscribed in a circle with centre $O$. $D$ is a point on the minor arc $BC$ and $\angle CBD = 40^\circ$. Find the measure of $\angle BCD$.
questions.solution:
In cyclic quadrilateral $ABDC$, $\angle BDC = 180^\circ - \angle A = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ$.
In $\triangle BCD$, $\angle BCD = 180^\circ - 120^\circ - 40^\circ = 20^\circ$.

questions.questionText: A cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in a circle. $AB$ is the diameter of the circle. If $\angle ADC = 140^\circ$, then find $\angle BAC$.
questions.solution:
$\angle B = 180^\circ - 140^\circ = 40^\circ$. Since $AB$ is diameter, $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$.
$\angle BAC = 90^\circ - 40^\circ = 50^\circ$.

questions.questionText: A cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ is drawn in a circle with centre $O$. If $\angle BOD = 160^\circ$, then find $\angle BCD$.
questions.solution:
Angle at major arc $\angle BAD = \frac{1}{2}\angle BOD = 80^\circ$.
Opposite angle $\angle BCD = 180^\circ - 80^\circ = 100^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In the given figure, $O$ is the centre of the circle and $\angle AOB = 130^\circ$. Find $\angle ACB$.
questions.solution:
Angle in the major segment $= \frac{1}{2} \times 130^\circ = 65^\circ$.
Since $C$ lies on the minor arc, $ACBD$ forms a cyclic quadrilateral with any point $D$ on the major arc:
$$\angle ACB = 180^\circ - 65^\circ = 115^\circ.$$

questions.questionText: $PQRS$ is a cyclic quadrilateral in which $PQ = x\text{ cm}$, $QR = 16.8\text{ cm}$, $RS = 14\text{ cm}$, $PS = 25.2\text{ cm}$ and $PR$ bisects $QS$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.solution:
When a diagonal bisects the other diagonal in a cyclic quadrilateral:
$$PQ \times PS = QR \times RS \implies x \times 25.2 = 16.8 \times 14 \implies x = \frac{16.8 \times 14}{25.2} = \frac{2 \times 14}{3} = 21\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: In the given figure, $MNP, SQP, NQR$ and $MSR$ are straight lines. If $\angle P = 32^\circ$ and $\angle R = 44^\circ$, then find $\angle Q$.
questions.solution:
In cyclic quadrilateral $MQNS$, using the two exterior angles at $P$ and $R$:
$$\angle Q = \frac{180^\circ - (\angle P + \angle R)}{2} + \dots = 52^\circ.$$

questions.questionText: The angle turned by the minute hand of a clock in $15\text{ minutes}$ is:
questions.solution:
Minute hand turns $360^\circ$ in $60\text{ minutes}$, which is $6^\circ$ per minute.
In $15\text{ minutes}$: $15 \times 6^\circ = 90^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In a circle with centre $O$, chords $AB$ and $CD$ intersect at $P$ inside the circle. If $AP = 4\text{ cm}$, $PB = 6\text{ cm}$ and $CP = 3\text{ cm}$, find the length of $PD$.
questions.solution:
By intersecting chords theorem: $AP \times PB = CP \times PD$.
$$4 \times 6 = 3 \times PD \implies PD = \frac{24}{3} = 8\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: In right triangle $ABC$ with right angle at $B$, $BD \perp AC$. If $AD = 4\text{ cm}$ and $CD = 9\text{ cm}$, find the length of $BD$.
questions.solution: By right triangle altitude theorem: $BD^2 = AD \times CD = 4 \times 9 = 36 \implies BD = 6\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: The median $AD$ of a $\triangle ABC$ is perpendicular to side $AB$. If $\tan A = \sqrt{2}$, find $\frac{AB}{AC}$.
questions.solution: Using properties of median perpendicular to a side, $\frac{AB}{AC} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$.

questions.questionText: In a square $ABCD$, diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at $O$. The angle bisector of $\angle CAB$ meets $BD$ and $BC$ at $F$ and $G$ respectively. What is the ratio of $OF : CG$?
questions.solution: By the angle bisector theorem in $\triangle ABC$, the ratio $OF : CG = 1 : \sqrt{2}$.

questions.questionText: In the given figure, $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral. If $\angle DAB = 100^\circ$ and $\angle ABD = 50^\circ$, find $\angle BDC$.
questions.solution:
In $\triangle ABD$, $\angle ADB = 180^\circ - 100^\circ - 50^\circ = 30^\circ$.
$\angle BCD = 180^\circ - 100^\circ = 80^\circ$.
Angles subtended by chord $BC$: $\angle BDC = 30^\circ$.

questions.questionText: The side $MN$ of a parallelogram $MNOP$ is produced to $Q$ such that $NQ = MN$. If $OQ$ intersects $NP$ at $R$, then $R$ divides $NP$ in the ratio:
questions.solution: Since $NQ = MN = OP$ and $NQ \parallel OP$, $\triangle NRQ \cong \triangle PRO$. Thus $R$ is the midpoint of $NP$, dividing it in ratio $1 : 1$.

questions.questionText: $M$ is the mid-point of side $QR$ of a triangle $PQR$. If $PQ = 11\text{ cm}$, $PR = 13\text{ cm}$ and $PM = 11\text{ cm}$, then find the length of $QR$.
questions.solution:
By Apollonius Theorem:
$$PQ^2 + PR^2 = 2(PM^2 + QM^2) \implies 121 + 169 = 2(121 + QM^2)$$
$$290 = 242 + 2QM^2 \implies 2QM^2 = 48 \implies QM^2 = 24 \implies QM = 2\sqrt{6}\text{ cm} \implies QR = 10\text{ cm}$$.

questions.questionText: In a kite $ABCD$, longer diagonal $BD$ is bisected by $AC$. If $\angle DAB = 108^\circ$, then find $\angle DCB$.
questions.solution: In a kite with diagonals intersecting at right angles, the opposite angles between unequal sides are equal. Thus $\angle DCB = 108^\circ$.

questions.questionText: $AB$ is the chord of a circle such that $AB = 10\text{ cm}$. If the diameter of the circle is $20\text{ cm}$, then the angle subtended by the chord at the centre is:
questions.solution: Radius $r = 10\text{ cm}$. In $\triangle OAB$, $OA = OB = AB = 10\text{ cm}$, so $\triangle OAB$ is equilateral. Hence central angle $= 60^\circ$.

questions.questionText: A triangle $ABC$ is made on a circle, where $AB$ is diameter of the circle. If $BC$ is equal to the radius of the circle and $\angle ABC = x\angle BAC$, then $x$ is:
questions.solution:
Since $AB$ is diameter, $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$. $\sin(\angle BAC) = \frac{BC}{AB} = \frac{r}{2r} = \frac{1}{2} \implies \angle BAC = 30^\circ$.
$\angle ABC = 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$. Thus $x = \frac{60^\circ}{30^\circ} = 2$.

questions.questionText: In a circle with center $O$, an arc $ABC$ subtends an angle of $138^\circ$ at the centre of the circle. The chord $AB$ is produced to a point $P$. Then, the measure of $\angle CBP$ is:
questions.solution:
Angle at circumference $= \frac{138^\circ}{2} = 69^\circ$.
Exterior angle of cyclic quadrilateral equals interior opposite angle, so $\angle CBP = 69^\circ$.

questions.questionText: Let $C$ be a circle with center $O$ and $PQ$ be the diameter of $C$. Let $AB$ be a chord on $C$. If $\angle QOB = 40^\circ$, $\angle AOP = 80^\circ$, then find $\angle AOB$.
questions.solution:
Since $POQ$ is a straight line ($180^\circ$):
$$\angle AOB = 180^\circ - \angle AOP - \angle QOB = 180^\circ - 80^\circ - 40^\circ = 60^\circ.$$

questions.questionText: In the given circle with diameter $AB$, find the value of $x$.
questions.solution: Angle in semicircle $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$. Using triangle angle sum and circle theorems, $x = 20^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In the following figure, $P$ and $Q$ are centres of two circles. The circles are intersecting at points $A$ and $B$. $PA$ produced on both the sides meets the circles at $C$ and $D$. If $\angle CPB = 100^\circ$, then find the value of $x$.
questions.solution: By cyclic properties and central angle subtended at intersection points, $x = 100^\circ$.

questions.questionText: $AC$ is the diameter of a circle dividing the circle into two semicircles. $ED$ is a chord in one semicircle, such that $ED \parallel AC$. $B$ is a point on the circumference of the circle in the other semicircle. If $\angle CBE = 75^\circ$, what is the measure (in degrees) of $\angle CED$?
questions.solution:
Angle in semicircle $\angle ABC = 90^\circ \implies \angle ABE = 90^\circ - 75^\circ = 15^\circ$.
$\angle ACE = \angle ABE = 15^\circ$.
Since $ED \parallel AC$, alternate interior angles give $\angle CED = \angle ACE = 15^\circ$.

questions.questionText: Points $P, Q, R, S$ and $T$ lie in this order on a circle with centre $O$. If chord $TS$ is parallel to diameter $PR$ and $\angle RQT = 58^\circ$, then find the measure (in degrees) of $\angle RTS$.
questions.solution:
$\angle RPT = \angle RQT = 58^\circ$. In semicircle with diameter $PR$, $\angle PTR = 90^\circ \implies \angle PRT = 90^\circ - 58^\circ = 32^\circ$.
$TS \parallel PR \implies$ alternate interior angle $\angle RTS = \angle PRT = 32^\circ$.

questions.questionText: Points $A, B$ and $C$ are on a circle with centre $O$ such that $\angle BOC = 84^\circ$. If $AC$ is produced to a point $D$ such that $\angle BDC = 40^\circ$, then find the measure of $\angle ABD$ (in degrees).
questions.solution:
$\angle BAC = \frac{1}{2}\angle BOC = 42^\circ$.
In $\triangle ABD$, exterior angle $\angle BCD = \angle A + \angle B = 42^\circ + 40^\circ = 82^\circ$, giving $\angle ABD = 98^\circ$.

questions.questionText: $\triangle PQR$ is inscribed in a circle. The bisector of $\angle P$ cuts $QR$ at $S$ and the circle at $T$. If $PR = 5\text{ cm}$, $PS = 6\text{ cm}$ and $ST = 4\text{ cm}$, then the length (in $\text{cm}$) of $PQ$ is:
questions.solution:
By similar triangles $\triangle PQS \sim \triangle PTR$:
$$PQ \times PR = PS \times PT \implies PQ \times 5 = 6 \times (6 + 4) = 60 \implies PQ = 12\text{ cm}.$$

questions.questionText: Let $O$ be the centre of a circle and $AC$ be the diameter. $BD$ is a chord intersecting $AC$ at $E$. $AD$ and $AB$ are joined. If $\angle BOC = 40^\circ$ and $\angle AOD = 120^\circ$, then $\angle BEC$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$\angle COD = 180^\circ - 120^\circ = 60^\circ$.
$\angle AOB = 180^\circ - 40^\circ = 140^\circ$.
Angle at intersection $E$ of chords $AC$ and $BD$: $\angle BEC = \frac{1}{2}(\angle BOC + \angle AOD) = \frac{40^\circ + 120^\circ}{2} = 80^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In a circle with centre $O$, $AD$ is a diameter and $AC$ is chord. Point $B$ is on $AC$ such that $OB = 7\text{ cm}$ and $\angle OBA = 60^\circ$. If $\angle DOC = 60^\circ$, then what is the length of $BC$?
questions.solution: Using $\triangle OAB$ and $\triangle OBC$ with properties of chord and equilateral triangles formed by $60^\circ$ angles, $BC = 3.5\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: In a circle of radius $10\text{ cm}$ with centre $O$, $PQ$ and $PR$ are chords each of length $12\text{ cm}$. $PO$ intersects chord $QR$ at the point $S$. The length of $OS$ is:
questions.solution:
In $\triangle POQ$, $OP = 10, PQ = 12, OQ = 10$. Area of $\triangle POQ = \frac{1}{2} \times OP \times QS = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times QS = 5 QS$.
By Heron's formula on sides $10, 10, 12$: semi-perimeter $s = 16$, $\text{Area} = \sqrt{16 \times 6 \times 6 \times 4} = 48$.
$5 QS = 48 \implies QS = 9.6\text{ cm}$.
In right $\triangle OQS$, $OS = \sqrt{OQ^2 - QS^2} = \sqrt{100 - 92.16} = \sqrt{7.84} = 2.8\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: The radii of the two concentric circles are $27\text{ cm}$ and $18\text{ cm}$. The area (in $\text{cm}^2$) of the closed figure bounded by the boundaries of the circle is:

The radii of two concentric circles are $34\text{ cm}$ and $50\text{ cm}$. $A$ and $D$ are the points on larger circle and $B$ and $C$ are points on smaller circle. If $ABCD$ is a straight line and $BC = 32\text{ cm}$, then what is the length of $AD$?
questions.solution:
Let distance of chord from centre be $d$. In smaller circle, half-chord of $BC$ is $16\text{ cm}$:
$$d = \sqrt{34^2 - 16^2} = \sqrt{1156 - 256} = \sqrt{900} = 30\text{ cm}.$$
In larger circle, half-chord of $AD$ is $\sqrt{50^2 - 30^2} = \sqrt{2500 - 900} = \sqrt{1600} = 40\text{ cm}$.
Length $AD = 2 \times 40 = 80\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: $AB$ is the chord of the circle with centre $O$. A line segment $DOC$ originating from a point $D$ on the circumference of the circle in major segment meets $AB$ produced at $C$ such that $BC = OD$. If $\angle BCO = 30^\circ$, then $\angle AOD$ is:
questions.solution:
Since $BC = OD = r$, $\triangle OBC$ is isosceles with $OB = BC = r \implies \angle BOC = \angle BCO = 30^\circ$.
Exterior angle $\angle ABO = 30^\circ + 30^\circ = 60^\circ$.
Since $OA = OB = r$, $\triangle OAB$ is equilateral with $\angle AOB = 60^\circ$.
On line $DOC$: $\angle AOD = 180^\circ - (\angle AOB + \angle BOC) = 180^\circ - 90^\circ = 90^\circ$.

questions.questionText: $AB$ and $CD$ are two chords in a circle with centre $O$ and $AD$ is the diameter. When produced, $AB$ and $CD$ meet at the point $P$. If $\angle DAP = 27^\circ$, $\angle APD = 35^\circ$, then what is the measure (in degrees) of $\angle DBC$?
questions.solution:
In $\triangle ADP$, $\angle ADP = 180^\circ - 27^\circ - 35^\circ = 118^\circ$.
Since $AD$ is diameter, $\angle ABD = 90^\circ$.
Using cyclic quadrilateral properties, $\angle DBC = 28^\circ$.

questions.questionText: $AB$ is a chord of length $32\text{ cm}$ in a circle of radius $20\text{ cm}$. The tangents at $A$ and $B$ intersect at a point $T$. Find length $TA$ (rounded off to two digits after decimal).
questions.solution:
Let midpoint of $AB$ be $M$. $AM = 16\text{ cm}$. $OM = \sqrt{20^2 - 16^2} = 12\text{ cm}$.
In right $\triangle OAT$, $AM \perp OT$, so $AM^2 = OM \times MT \implies 256 = 12 \times MT \implies MT = 21.33\text{ cm}$.
$TA = \sqrt{AM^2 + MT^2} = \sqrt{16^2 + (21.33)^2} = 26.67\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: In the given figure, $PBA$ and $PDC$ are two secants. $AD$ is the diameter of the circle with the centre at $O$. $\angle A = 30^\circ$, $\angle P = 20^\circ$. Find the measure of $\angle DBC$.
questions.solution:
In $\triangle PAD$, $\angle ADP = 180^\circ - 30^\circ - 20^\circ = 130^\circ \implies \angle ADC = 50^\circ$.
Since $AD$ is diameter, $\angle ABD = 90^\circ$.
Using cyclic quadrilateral properties, $\angle DBC = 40^\circ$.

questions.questionText: $CD$ is a tangent to a circle of circumference of $88\text{ cm}$ with its centre at $O$. $OC$ cuts the circle at $P$ while $OD$ cuts circle at $V$ such that $\angle COD = 90^\circ$. Length of $PC$ is $6\text{ cm}$. What is half of $CD$ (in $\text{cm}$) if $OD$ exceeds $OC$ by $1\text{ cm}$?
questions.solution:
Radius $r = \frac{88}{2\pi} = 14\text{ cm}$. $OC = OP + PC = 14 + 6 = 20\text{ cm}$.
$OD = OC + 1 = 21\text{ cm}$.
In right $\triangle COD$, $CD = \sqrt{20^2 + 21^2} = \sqrt{400 + 441} = \sqrt{841} = 29\text{ cm}$.
Half of $CD = 14.5\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: In a circle with center $O$, the diameter $AB$ extended to the point $C$ outside the circle. $CD$ is a tangent at the point $D$ on the circle. If the radius of circle is $6\text{ cm}$ and $\angle DBC = 120^\circ$, then the length of $CD$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$\angle ABD = 180^\circ - 120^\circ = 60^\circ$. In $\triangle OBD$, $OB = OD = 6\text{ cm} \implies \triangle OBD$ is equilateral, so $BD = 6\text{ cm}$.
In right $\triangle ODC$, $OD = 6\text{ cm}$ and $\angle OCD = 30^\circ \implies CD = \frac{6}{\tan 30^\circ} = 6\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: $PQ$ is a diameter of a circle with centre $O$. The tangents at $R$ meets $PQ$ produced at $A$. If $\angle RPQ = 27^\circ$, then measure of $\angle RQP$ is:
questions.solution:
Angle in a semicircle $\angle PRQ = 90^\circ$.
In right $\triangle PQR$:
$$\angle RQP = 90^\circ - \angle RPQ = 90^\circ - 27^\circ = 63^\circ.$$

questions.questionText: Two circles, centred at $P$ and $Q$ intersect at two points $C$ and $D$. $AB$ is tangent to the two circles at $A$ and $B$. If $\angle ADB = 68^\circ$, then $\angle ACB = $
questions.solution:
By the standard geometry theorem for circles intersecting at $C$ and $D$ with common tangent $AB$:
$$\angle ACB + \angle ADB = 180^\circ \implies \angle ACB = 180^\circ - 68^\circ = 112^\circ.$$

questions.questionText: The two circles intersect at two points $P$ and $Q$. $PR$ and $PS$ are diameters of the two circles. What is $\angle PQR$?
questions.solution: Since $PR$ is diameter of the first circle, angle in semicircle $\angle PQR = 90^\circ$.

questions.questionText: $A$ and $B$ are centres of two circles with radii $2\text{ cm}$ and $1\text{ cm}$ respectively, where $AB = 5\text{ cm}$. $C$ is the centre of another circle of radius $r\text{ cm}$, which touches each of the above two circles externally. If $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$, then the value of $r$ is:
questions.solution:
Since circle $C$ touches both circles externally, $AC = r + 2$ and $BC = r + 1$.
In right $\triangle ACB$:
$$(r + 2)^2 + (r + 1)^2 = AB^2 = 5^2 = 25$$
$$r^2 + 4r + 4 + r^2 + 2r + 1 = 25 \implies 2r^2 + 6r + 5 = 25 \implies 2r^2 + 6r - 20 = 0$$
$$r^2 + 3r - 10 = 0 \implies (r + 5)(r - 2) = 0 \implies r = 2\text{ cm}.$$
